full_prose_under_review.title: Massachusetts Pharmacy Change Filings: Name, Ownership, Manager, Remodel, Relocation
full_prose_under_review.topic: Pharmacy licensure / Changes to an already licensed pharmacy
full_prose_under_review.subtopic: Which changes need prior Board approval, which need notice, on what clock, and the suitability screen behind a change of owner
learning_objectives: Sort a change to an operating pharmacy into the prior-approval family or the notice family before reaching for any number.
State the 14-day, 14-day and 90-day clocks in 247 CMR 6.12, 6.11 and 6.16 and say which direction each one runs.
Identify the two changes that carry an express prohibition on acting before the Board approves.
Name who owes each filing, and why a transfer of ownership generates two independent duties rather than one.
List what each application must carry, and distinguish the relocation drawings from the remodeling drawings.
Explain how the 247 CMR 6.03 suitability factors reach beyond the named applicant and beyond Massachusetts pharmacies.

orientation.text: A Massachusetts pharmacy licence is not a general permission to operate; it describes one particular pharmacy, trading under a stated name, owned by a stated licensee, managed by a named Manager of Record, occupying a described footprint at a stated address. Every requirement in this section follows from that. When one of those facts changes, the licence on file stops describing the pharmacy that actually exists, and 247 CMR 6.00 requires the licensee either to tell the Board what happened or to ask the Board first. The whole topic is learned by asking, of any change, which of those two the Board demands, and the answer is not intuitive: a rebrand that changes nothing physical still generates a filing, while a move of two doors along cannot lawfully happen at all until the Board says yes.

The prior-approval family is defined by a prohibition rather than by a deadline. Under 247 CMR 6.16 a licensed pharmacy shall apply to the Board for approval to relocate to a new address prior to relocating and may not relocate until it receives approval, and its application is submitted at least 90 days before the desired date of relocation unless the Board approves otherwise. Under 247 CMR 6.15(1) the listed pharmacy types shall apply for approval to remodel or to change the configuration or square footage and may not commence any construction work or remodeling until approval arrives. Read those two clauses closely: the sanctionable act is moving or breaking ground, not missing a deadline. Filing the application does not authorise anything, and 247 CMR 6.15 attaches no day count at all, so a pharmacy that files on the morning the contractor arrives has satisfied the form of the requirement and violated its substance. A change of Manager of Record sits in the same family in a quieter way: 247 CMR 6.10(1) requires the pharmacy to submit its application to the Board for approval whenever there is a change, and states no day count of its own.

The notice family carries the numbers, and the two 14-day clocks run in opposite directions. 247 CMR 6.12 is titled Notifications, but the only change it reaches is the operating name: a licensee shall notify the Board, within 14 days, in writing, of any change in the name under which the pharmacy operates, accompanied by appropriate authorizing documentation. That clock starts at the change and runs forward, and the documentation is part of the notice rather than something to follow later. 247 CMR 6.11(1) runs the other way: at least 14 days before the transfer of ownership of a licensed pharmacy the licensee shall notify the Board of the proposed transfer, so the deadline sits in the past by the time the sale closes. A transfer is also the one change that generates two independent duties on the same clock, because 247 CMR 6.11(2) separately requires the proposed new licensee to submit an application for a licence to operate a pharmacy at least 14 days before the transfer. Neither filing answers the other.

Behind the paperwork sit two things the Board is protecting, and naming them makes the requirements cohere. The first is who stands behind the licence. A transfer of ownership is not a records update but an application, and 247 CMR 6.11(4) lets the Board find the proposed new licensee and any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the factors in 247 CMR 6.03. Those eleven factors reach an applicant, a licensee or an interest holder, count conduct at any pharmacy, health care facility or other entity registered by the FDA or the DEA rather than Massachusetts pharmacies alone, and include one item that is a status rather than misconduct: that the person has prescriptive privileges. The second is the controlled substance stock, which is the part of a pharmacy that cannot be allowed to change hands unwitnessed. That is why the change of Manager of Record application under 247 CMR 6.10(2)(a) carries an attestation that an inventory was performed and filed, signed by both the outgoing and the incoming Manager, and why the incoming owner's application under 247 CMR 6.11(3) carries a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances together with the inventory report required by 247 CMR 6.14.

comparison_tables.title: How far the 247 CMR 6.03 suitability factors reach

cells: Which persons do the factors reach?
Each factor is framed as reaching an applicant, a licensee or an interest holder, so a minority investor is inside the inquiry even though the company is the named applicant
Whose history counts?
Conduct at a pharmacy, a health care facility, or any other entity registered by the FDA or the DEA that the person owned, operated or held an interest in, not Massachusetts pharmacies alone
Is every listed factor a form of misconduct?
No. One listed factor is that the applicant, licensee or interest holder has prescriptive privileges, which is a status and not a finding of wrongdoing
Does a matter resolved without a finding count?
Yes. A consent agreement resolving a complaint that resulted in disciplinary action is among the listed factors, alongside discipline, suspension, denial or revocation
When do the factors bite on a change of owner?
On the incoming application: 247 CMR 6.11(4) lets the Board find the proposed new licensee and any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts Drug Store pharmacy signs a lease on a larger unit in the same shopping centre and intends to move over a weekend six weeks from now. The district manager says the pharmacy will write to the Board within 14 days of the move, the way it did last year when the chain rebranded. What does 247 CMR 6.00 actually require?
steps: Classify the change before reaching for a number. A move to a new address is governed by 247 CMR 6.16, which is an approval provision, not a notification provision.

Read the prohibition in 6.16: the pharmacy shall apply for approval prior to relocating and may not relocate until it receives approval from the Board. Six weeks of planning is irrelevant if approval has not arrived.
Read the lead time: the application is submitted at least 90 days before the desired date of relocation, unless otherwise approved by the Board. Six weeks is inside that minimum.

Check what the application carries: an application with payment of the appropriate fee, blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, and any other information the Board requires.

Trace where the 14-day idea came from. 247 CMR 6.12 sets 14 days for a change in the name under which the pharmacy operates, which is a different change under a different section, and it says nothing about premises.
worked_examples.resolution: The pharmacy must apply at least 90 days ahead and may not move until the Board approves. The error the scenario invites is borrowing the familiar 14-day notice clock from the name-change provision and treating a relocation as something to report after it has happened.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacy is being sold. Twenty days before the closing date the buyer submits a complete licence application with an inventory report and the bill of sale. The seller files nothing, reasoning that the buyer's application already tells the Board everything about the transaction and that the licence will simply follow the business across.
steps: Separate the two duties in 247 CMR 6.11. Paragraph (1) is owed by the licensee: at least 14 days before the transfer it shall notify the Board of the proposed transfer of ownership.

Paragraph (2) is owed by the proposed new licensee: at least 14 days before the transfer it shall submit an application for a licence to operate a pharmacy. The buyer's timely filing satisfies its own duty and nothing else.

Note what the seller owes besides the notice: 247 CMR 6.11(1) directs the outgoing licensee to comply with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13, the notification and closing provisions, which are covered separately.

Check the buyer's application against 247 CMR 6.11(3): a complete application, a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances, the inventory report required by 247 CMR 6.14, the official bill of sale, and anything else the Board requires.

Notice what the buyer is actually asking for. This is an application the Board may refuse, and under 247 CMR 6.11(4) it may find the proposed new licensee or any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors.
worked_examples.resolution: The seller's position is unsound on both limbs. The error is treating a sale as one transaction with one filing, and assuming the licence passes with the business when what actually happens is that a new applicant asks the Board for a licence of its own.

worked_examples.scenario: A Manager of Record is terminated on a Friday and refuses to return to the pharmacy. The owner wants to file the change of Manager of Record application on Monday with a staff pharmacist signing the inventory attestation in the departed manager's place, and asks whether the inventory can be limited to Schedules II through V.
steps: Start with the default in 247 CMR 6.10(2)(a): the attestation confirming the pharmacy performed an inventory and filed the report with its controlled substance records is signed by the outgoing Manager of Record and the proposed incoming Manager of Record.

Check whether the substitution route is open. A staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign only where the outgoing Manager is unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, and termination is one of the three listed grounds, so it is available here.
Attach the condition: the Board must be notified at the time the application is submitted of the reason the staff pharmacist is signing. The substitution is not silent.

Answer the scope question. The inventory covers all controlled substances in Schedules II through V and Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program, so limiting it to II through V is short.

Assemble the rest of the application under 247 CMR 6.10(2): the original Drug Store Pharmacy licence, the required fees, and any additional information the Board requires. Expect that the Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it.
worked_examples.resolution: The staff pharmacist may sign because termination is one of the three listed grounds, provided the reason is given to the Board with the application, and the inventory must reach reportable Schedule VI. The errors invited here are treating the substitution as generally available for an uncooperative manager, and stopping the count at Schedule V.

worked_examples.scenario: A Drug Store pharmacy is enlarging its prescription area by taking in an adjoining storeroom. The contractor is booked for Monday morning, and the pharmacy files its application first thing Monday, enclosing drawings of the enlarged prescription area. The owner reasons that the application is in and that work can stop if the Board objects.
steps: Identify the provision. Taking in a storeroom changes both the configuration and the square footage, which is squarely within 247 CMR 6.15(1).

Read the prohibition rather than a deadline: the pharmacy may not commence any construction work or remodeling until it receives approval from the Board. Filing on Monday morning does not license Monday morning's work.

Test the drawings against 247 CMR 6.15(3)(a), which requires blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, the prescription area and the counseling area. Drawings of the prescription area alone are incomplete.
Add the Massachusetts-only item under 247 CMR 6.15(3)(b): a written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation, required if the pharmacy is located in Massachusetts.

Compare this with a relocation application, which under 247 CMR 6.16 asks for drawings depicting the pharmacy layout and the fee, and does not call for the counseling area or the transport security plan.
worked_examples.resolution: Two things are wrong: work may not start before approval, and the drawings omit the counseling area, with the transport security plan missing as well. The error the scenario invites is treating the act of filing as the trigger, so that a pending application feels like permission.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A licensee shall notify the Board of a change in the name under which the pharmacy operates within ______, in ______, accompanied by ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 14 days; writing; appropriate authorizing documentation (247 CMR 6.12).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A relocation application must be submitted at least ______ before the desired date of relocation, unless ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 90 days; otherwise approved by the Board (247 CMR 6.16).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: On a transfer of ownership the licensee must notify the Board at least ______ before the transfer, and the proposed new licensee must submit its licence application at least ______ before the transfer.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 14 days; 14 days. It is the same period, owed independently by each side under 247 CMR 6.11(1) and (2).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which two changes carry an express prohibition on acting before the Board approves, and what is each prohibited from doing?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Relocation, where the pharmacy may not relocate until it receives approval (247 CMR 6.16); and remodeling or a change of configuration or square footage, where it may not commence any construction work or remodeling until it receives approval (247 CMR 6.15(1)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Remodeling drawings under 247 CMR 6.15(3)(a) must depict the pharmacy layout, the ______ area and the ______ area.
retrieval_prompts.answer: prescription; counseling.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which item does a remodeling application require of a pharmacy located in Massachusetts that 247 CMR 6.16 does not ask of a relocating pharmacy?
retrieval_prompts.answer: A written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The change of Manager of Record inventory attestation is normally signed by ______ and ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: the outgoing Manager of Record; the proposed incoming Manager of Record (247 CMR 6.10(2)(a)).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign the inventory report only where the outgoing Manager of Record is unavailable due to ______, ______ or ______, and provided ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: death; serious illness; termination; the Board is notified at the time the application is submitted of the reason the staff pharmacist is signing.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The inventory behind a change of Manager of Record covers all controlled substances in Schedules ______ and also ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: II through V; Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Besides the complete application, name the three items 247 CMR 6.11(3) requires from the proposed new licensee.
retrieval_prompts.answer: A description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances; an inventory report of controlled substances required by 247 CMR 6.14; and an official bill of sale.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The 247 CMR 6.03 suitability factors are framed as reaching an applicant, a licensee or ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: an interest holder.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which listed 247 CMR 6.03 factor is a status rather than a form of misconduct?
retrieval_prompts.answer: That the applicant, licensee or interest holder has prescriptive privileges.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which change to an operating pharmacy has a filing requirement but no day count stated in its own section?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Both the change of Manager of Record (247 CMR 6.10) and remodeling or a change of configuration or square footage (247 CMR 6.15) require an application for approval without stating a number of days.

quick_review.text: 247 CMR 6.12 is headed Notifications, but the only change it reaches is the name under which the pharmacy operates: written notice to the Board within 14 days, with appropriate authorizing documentation.

A transfer of ownership generates two duties on the same 14-day clock: the licensee notifies the Board of the proposed transfer, and the proposed new licensee submits an application for a licence to operate a pharmacy.
The outgoing licensee on a transfer must also comply with 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13, the notification and closing provisions.

The incoming licensee's application carries a complete application, a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances, the inventory report required by 247 CMR 6.14, an official bill of sale, and anything else the Board requires.

A pharmacy may not relocate until it receives Board approval, and applies at least 90 days before the desired relocation date unless the Board approves otherwise, with the fee and drawings depicting the pharmacy layout.

A pharmacy may not commence any construction work or remodeling until the Board approves a remodel or a change of configuration or square footage; the drawings must show layout, prescription area and counseling area.
A Massachusetts pharmacy remodeling also submits a written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation.

A change of Manager of Record is an application to the Board for approval, carrying a dual-signed inventory attestation, the original Drug Store Pharmacy licence and the required fees; the Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it.
The 247 CMR 6.03 suitability factors are the Board's discretionary grounds for concluding that licensing an applicant or licensee would not be in the interest of public health, safety and welfare.

decision_logic.condition: A fact about an operating pharmacy is about to change.
decision_logic.action: Ask first whether the section governing it is an approval provision or a notification provision, and only then look for a number. Relocation, remodeling and a change of Manager of Record are approvals; a name change is a notice.

decision_logic.condition: The change is the name under which the pharmacy operates.
decision_logic.action: Notify the Board in writing within 14 days of the change and send the appropriate authorizing documentation with the notice, whether or not the licensee, the premises and the ownership are unchanged.

File the licensee's own notice of the proposed transfer at least 14 days before it, and confirm separately that the proposed new licensee has filed its own application at least 14 days before the transfer. Do not let either filing stand in for the other.

decision_logic.condition: You are the incoming owner or the incoming Manager of Record.
decision_logic.action: Assemble the controlled substance paperwork the section names: the transfer description and 247 CMR 6.14 inventory report with the bill of sale for a change of owner, and the dual-signed inventory attestation with the original licence for a change of Manager.

decision_logic.condition: The outgoing Manager of Record will not or cannot sign the attestation.
decision_logic.action: Check the reason against the three listed grounds of death, serious illness and termination. If one applies, authorise a staff pharmacist and tell the Board the reason at the time the application is submitted; if none applies, the substitution is not open.

decision_logic.condition: Construction, reconfiguration or a change of square footage is planned.
decision_logic.action: Stop work until approval arrives, and check the drawings for the counseling area as well as the layout and the prescription area, adding the written transport security plan for a Massachusetts pharmacy.

decision_logic.condition: A move to a new address is planned.
decision_logic.action: Count back at least 90 days from the desired relocation date and file the application with the fee and layout drawings, and do not relocate until the Board approves.

decision_logic.condition: The question asks what the Board may do with an application rather than what a licensee must file.
decision_logic.action: Reach for the 247 CMR 6.03 factors, and remember that they reach an interest holder as well as the applicant, and count history at any FDA- or DEA-registered entity.

ma_vs_federal.text: These are Massachusetts licensure provisions in 247 CMR 6.00. Federal law enters only as a reference point inside the suitability inquiry, where 247 CMR 6.03 counts a person's history at a pharmacy, health care facility or other entity registered by the FDA or the DEA, so out-of-state and non-pharmacy federal registrants are inside a Massachusetts question.

The controlled substance paperwork these sections require is Board-facing rather than a federal filing: 247 CMR 6.10(2)(a) has the inventory report filed with the pharmacy's own controlled substance records and attested to the Board, and 247 CMR 6.11(3) makes the transfer description and the inventory report components of a Board application.

exceptions.text: The 90-day relocation lead time yields to the Board: 247 CMR 6.16 states it unless otherwise approved by the Board. The prohibition on relocating before approval carries no such qualifier.

The dual-signature attestation has exactly one substitution route: a staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign where the outgoing Manager of Record is unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, provided the Board is notified at the time of application of the reason.
The written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation is required under 247 CMR 6.15(3)(b) only if the pharmacy is located in Massachusetts.
247 CMR 6.15(1) names the pharmacy types it reaches, and the only non-resident pharmacy on that list is a non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy.

timing_deadlines.event: Change in the name under which the pharmacy operates
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 14 days, in writing, running forward from the change
timing_deadlines.consequence: The notice must be accompanied by appropriate authorizing documentation, so a bare letter does not discharge 247 CMR 6.12, and waiting for the next renewal is out of time.

timing_deadlines.event: Transfer of ownership, the licensee's notice
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the transfer
timing_deadlines.consequence: The clock runs backwards from the closing date and the duty is the outgoing licensee's own; the buyer's filing does not answer it.

timing_deadlines.event: Transfer of ownership, the proposed new licensee's application
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the transfer
timing_deadlines.consequence: This is an application to be granted rather than a notice to be logged: the Board may find the proposed new licensee and any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: Application at least 90 days before the desired date of relocation, unless otherwise approved by the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: The 90 days is a minimum lead time, not the whole duty: the pharmacy may not relocate until it receives approval.

timing_deadlines.event: Remodeling, or a change of configuration or square footage
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No day count is stated in 247 CMR 6.15
timing_deadlines.consequence: The controlling constraint is the prohibition instead: no construction work or remodeling may commence until the Board approves.

timing_deadlines.event: Change of Manager of Record at a resident pharmacy
timing_deadlines.timeframe: No day count is stated in 247 CMR 6.10; the application is submitted whenever there is a change
timing_deadlines.consequence: The application is for approval, and the Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it prior to approving or denying.

forms_records.text: Name change: written notice to the Board accompanied by appropriate authorizing documentation.

Transfer of ownership, incoming side: a complete application under 247 CMR 6.04 and 6.05 through 6.09, a description of the date and procedure to transfer controlled substances, an inventory report of controlled substances required by 247 CMR 6.14, an official bill of sale, and any additional information the Board requires.

Change of Manager of Record: an inventory attestation signed by the outgoing and the proposed incoming Manager of Record, the original Drug Store Pharmacy licence, required fees, and any additional information the Board requires. The application itself is signed by the licensee or its authorised representative and the proposed new Manager of Record.
Relocation: an application with payment of the appropriate fee, blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, and any other information the Board requires.

Remodeling or a change of configuration or square footage: blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, the prescription area and the counseling area; a written plan to maintain security of controlled substances during any transportation for a pharmacy located in Massachusetts; and any other information the Board requires.
The change of Manager of Record inventory report is filed with the pharmacy's own controlled substance records, and the attestation confirms to the Board that this was done.

role_duties.duty: Notify the Board in writing within 14 days of any change in the name under which the pharmacy operates, with appropriate authorizing documentation.

role_duties.role: Licensee, outgoing owner on a transfer
role_duties.duty: Notify the Board of the proposed transfer of ownership at least 14 days before it, and comply with the notification and closing provisions in 247 CMR 6.12 and 247 CMR 6.13.

Submit an application for a licence to operate a pharmacy at least 14 days before the transfer, supported by the complete application, the controlled substance transfer description, the 247 CMR 6.14 inventory report and the official bill of sale.
Stand to be assessed on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors alongside the proposed new licensee, even though the interest holder is not the named applicant.
Sign the attestation confirming the controlled substance inventory was performed and filed, unless unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination.
Sign both the change of Manager of Record application and the inventory attestation, and appear before the Board if it so requires.
Obtain Board approval before commencing any construction work or remodeling, and file drawings showing the layout, the prescription area and the counseling area.
Apply at least 90 days before the desired relocation date and wait for Board approval before relocating.
Decide, in its discretion and on the listed factors, whether an applicant, licensee or interest holder is suitable to establish or maintain a pharmacy.

common_traps.text: Importing the 14-day notice clock into a relocation or a remodel. Both are approvals with an express prohibition on acting first, and 247 CMR 6.16 sets 90 days while 247 CMR 6.15 sets no day count at all.
Reading the heading of 247 CMR 6.12, Notifications, as covering every change to a pharmacy. The only change it reaches is the name under which the pharmacy operates.
Treating a rebrand as cosmetic because the licence holder, the premises and the ownership are all unchanged, and reporting it at the next renewal.
Treating the buyer's application as discharging the seller's notice, or assuming the licence passes with the business rather than the buyer applying for one.

Believing that filing the remodel application is itself the permission, so that work may begin while the application is pending, and submitting drawings without the counseling area or the transport security plan.
Using the staff-pharmacist substitution for an outgoing Manager of Record who is merely unwilling, or omitting reportable Schedule VI substances from the inventory behind the attestation.
Reading the 247 CMR 6.03 factors as reaching only the named applicant and only Massachusetts pharmacy history, or assuming every listed factor describes misconduct.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A licensee shall NOTIFY THE BOARD, WITHIN 14 DAYS, IN WRITING, of any change in the NAME UNDER WHICH THE PHARMACY OPERATES, accompanied by APPROPRIATE AUTHORIZING DOCUMENTATION. The clock runs from the change and the notice must carry the supporting documentation.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: At least 14 days before the transfer of ownership of a licensed pharmacy the LICENSEE shall notify the Board of the proposed transfer, and the outgoing licensee shall comply with the notification and closing provisions and with the controlled substance distribution provisions. At least 14 days before the transfer the PROPOSED NEW LICENSEE shall submit an application to operate a pharmacy, supported by a complete application, a controlled substance inventory report required by 247 CMR 6.14, an official bill of sale, and any additional information the Board requires. The Board may find the proposed new licensee or any proposed new interest holder unsuitable on the 247 CMR 6.03 factors.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A change of Manager of Record application shall include an ATTESTATION confirming the pharmacy performed an inventory of all controlled substances in Schedules II through V AND Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program, and filed the inventory report with the pharmacy's controlled substance records. The attestation shall be SIGNED BY THE OUTGOING MANAGER OF RECORD AND THE PROPOSED INCOMING MANAGER OF RECORD. Where the outgoing Manager is unavailable due to DEATH, SERIOUS ILLNESS OR TERMINATION, a staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign PROVIDED the Board is notified at the time of application of the reason. The application also carries the ORIGINAL Drug Store Pharmacy licence and the required fees, and the Board may require the proposed Manager to appear before it.
exceptions: A staff pharmacist may sign where the outgoing Manager of Record is unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, on notice to the Board of the reason

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A pharmacy licensed by the Board shall APPLY TO THE BOARD FOR APPROVAL TO RELOCATE to a new address PRIOR TO RELOCATING and MAY NOT RELOCATE UNTIL IT RECEIVES APPROVAL. The application is submitted AT LEAST 90 DAYS before the desired date of relocation, unless otherwise approved by the Board, with the appropriate fee and blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A Drug Store pharmacy, sterile compounding pharmacy, complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy, institutional sterile compounding pharmacy and non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy shall apply to the Board for approval to remodel or to change the CONFIGURATION or SQUARE FOOTAGE, and MAY NOT COMMENCE ANY CONSTRUCTION WORK OR REMODELING until it receives approval. The supporting submission includes blueprints or equivalent architectural drawings depicting the pharmacy layout, the PRESCRIPTION AREA and the COUNSELING AREA, and, for a Massachusetts pharmacy, a WRITTEN PLAN TO MAINTAIN SECURITY OF CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES DURING ANY TRANSPORTATION.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: In its discretion the Board may determine an applicant or licensee is not suitable to establish or maintain a pharmacy and that issuing a licence would not be in the interest of public health, safety and welfare. The eleven listed factors reach an APPLICANT, LICENSEE OR INTEREST HOLDER and cover conduct presenting an immediate or serious threat to public health and safety; impeding Board or Department enforcement; assuming ownership to circumvent 247 CMR 2.00; prior discipline, denial or revocation, or a consent agreement resolving a complaint, at any pharmacy, health care facility or other FDA- or DEA-registered entity the person owned, operated or held an interest in; operating such an entity so as to create an immediate or serious threat; failure to demonstrate competence or experience to operate a pharmacy; obtaining or attempting to obtain a licence by fraud or misrepresentation; HOLDING PRESCRIPTIVE PRIVILEGES; and prior discipline or a consent agreement on a professional licence.

full_prose_under_review.title: Closing a Massachusetts Pharmacy: Board Notice, Patients, and the Controlled Stock
full_prose_under_review.topic: Pharmacy licensure / Closing a pharmacy under 247 CMR 6.13 and 6.14
full_prose_under_review.subtopic: The advance certified notice to the Board, the duties owed to patients, the post-closure surrender and attestation, how each of those varies with the type of pharmacy, and the separate procedure for moving controlled stock to another Board-licensed pharmacy
learning_objectives: Separate the three duties a closure sets running, to the Board, to patients and over the controlled stock, and name the audience each answers to.
State which closure clocks run backwards from the closure date and which single clock runs forwards from it.
List the six particulars 247 CMR 6.13(1) requires in the closure notice and the three of them that 247 CMR 6.13(2) drops for a non-resident pharmacy.
Identify the pharmacy types that must name a Board-licensed pharmacy suitable and available to provide continuity of care, and the one type that 247 CMR 6.13(7) excuses.

Work 247 CMR 6.14 through in order: the 14-day certified notice, the transfer-date inventory, the two Manager of Record signatures, the ten-day attestation, the two-year retention and the closing bar on possession.
Tell the closure attestation under 247 CMR 6.13(6)(b) apart from the transfer attestation under 247 CMR 6.14(2)(d).

orientation.text: Closing a pharmacy is not one duty with one deadline. It is a bundle of duties that run in parallel, each answering to a different audience, and a candidate who learns only the headline number will get the sequence wrong. The Board is owed advance written notice that the licence is about to stop being used. The patients who have been getting their prescriptions there are owed notice of their own and a route to their records. The controlled stock is owed an account of where it went. Nothing in 247 CMR 6.13 makes any of these three the precondition of the others in the sense of coming first; they overlap, and the regulation actually wires them together, because the notice sent to the Board has to report on what has already been done for the patients and on what is planned for the drugs.

Take the Board-facing duty first. Under 247 CMR 6.13(1) a Massachusetts pharmacy and a Manager of Record who intend to close shall officially notify the Board in writing, by certified mail, at least 14 days before the intended closure, unless otherwise authorized by the Board, and shall supply six particulars: the pharmacy's name, address and telephone number; the pharmacy licence and controlled substance registration numbers; the name of the pharmacist Manager of Record; the date the intended closure will take place; verification that adequate advance notice of the closure has been given to customers in accordance with 247 CMR 6.13(4); and the intended procedures for disposal or transfer of controlled substances. The last two are the interesting ones. A closure notice that identifies the pharmacy but says nothing about the customers or the drugs is incomplete on the day it is posted, which is why the patient work cannot be left until the final week.

The patient-facing duty has its own shape. 247 CMR 6.13(4) requires a licensee or a Manager of Record to identify each patient who had a prescription filled at the pharmacy within the preceding 90 days of the intended closure date, and then to attempt to notify each such patient at least 14 days prior to the closure date, by first class mail or other Board approved method. The verb is attempt, not achieve, and that is why a second, cruder instrument sits beside it: a notice posted in a conspicuous location at the pharmacy telling patients of the intended closure and of the procedure for requesting a transfer of patient file information. 247 CMR 6.13(5) then supplies the mechanism the posted notice advertises: upon patient request, or as law or contract requires, the files go to another pharmacy in a timely manner to meet patient needs. The 90 days is a look-back that fixes who is owed the letter; it is not a deadline of any kind.

The controlled stock is handled separately from everything else because it is not ordinary inventory that can simply leave with the fixtures. The pharmacy holds it under a controlled substance registration, and the Board wants that registration back together with proof of where the drugs went. So 247 CMR 6.13(6) sets the one closure clock that runs after the doors shut: within 14 days of closure the licensee and Manager of Record submit the original licence or licences and the controlled substances registration, plus an attestation that all controlled substances have been disposed of in accordance with the federal disposal regulation the subsection names, or transferred in accordance with 21 CFR 1301.52 and 247 CMR 6.14. Everything else about closure is done before the date; this is the piece that is proved afterwards. And the attestation is a fork, not a formality: it asks which of two routes the stock actually travelled.

If the answer is transfer to another pharmacy licensed by the Board, then 247 CMR 6.14 takes over and imposes a procedure with three clocks of its own. A licensee, Manager of Record or agent notifies the Board in writing by certified mail at least 14 days before the intended transfer of Schedules II through VI, unless otherwise authorized, naming both pharmacies, both sets of licence and registration numbers, both Managers of Record, the date the transfer will take place and the security procedures for it. No sooner than 14 days after that notification the transfer may proceed, and on the transfer date the transferor takes a complete inventory reaching Schedules II through V and every Schedule VI substance required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program. Both Managers of Record sign the report, both pharmacies file an attestation with the Board within ten days of the transfer, both keep a readily retrievable copy for at least two years, and the transferor may not possess any controlled substances after the date of transfer.

Finally, none of this is a single uniform checklist, and that is the point the regulation is easiest to get wrong on. A non-resident pharmacy gives the same 14-day certified notice under 247 CMR 6.13(2) but with a visibly shorter list of particulars, and the post-closure surrender and attestation in 247 CMR 6.13(6) is expressly stated not to apply to non-resident pharmacies at all. A sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding or non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy carries an extra duty under 247 CMR 6.13(3): at least 14 days ahead it must tell the Board the identity of a pharmacy licensed by the Board that is suitable and available to provide continuity of care to the closing pharmacy's patients. And 247 CMR 6.13(7) then subtracts, naming 247 CMR 6.13(3) and 247 CMR 6.13(4) as not required for institutional sterile compounding pharmacies. Reading the type before reading the duty is the habit this section is trying to build.

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts drug store pharmacy has set a closure date 20 days out. The Manager of Record drafts the certified letter to the Board giving the pharmacy's name, address and telephone number, its pharmacy licence and controlled substance registration numbers, her own name and the closure date, and plans to write to patients during the final week so that the letters arrive close to the date and are not forgotten. What is wrong with the plan?
steps: Check the draft against the six particulars in 247 CMR 6.13(1). Four are present. Two are missing: subparagraph (e), verification that adequate advance notice of the closure has been given to customers in accordance with 247 CMR 6.13(4), and subparagraph (f), the intended procedures for disposal or transfer of controlled substances.

Notice what subparagraph (e) does to the sequencing. It asks the pharmacy to verify a thing already done, so patient notice cannot be scheduled after the Board notice; a letter sent 20 days out cannot verify an attempt planned for day 15.

Fix the patient population from 247 CMR 6.13(4): each patient who had a prescription filled at the pharmacy within the preceding 90 days of the intended closure date, with the attempt made at least 14 days prior to the closure date by first class mail or other Board approved method.

Add the conspicuous posted notice, which must state the intended closure and the procedure for requesting a transfer of patient file information, and be ready to move files under 247 CMR 6.13(5) on request or as law or contract requires.
Decide now, not later, what happens to the controlled stock, because subparagraph (f) requires the intended disposal or transfer procedures to be stated in the same letter.
worked_examples.resolution: The plan treats the three closure duties as running in sequence when 247 CMR 6.13 runs them in parallel. That is the error the fact pattern invites: because the Board notice must itself verify the customer notice and describe the controlled-substance procedures, deferring the patient letters to the final week makes the 14-day Board notice incomplete on the day it is sent.

worked_examples.scenario: An institutional sterile compounding pharmacy licensed in Massachusetts will close next month. Its director reads 247 CMR 6.13(3), sees institutional sterile compounding pharmacies in the list, and starts hunting for a Board-licensed pharmacy to name for continuity of care while an assistant begins assembling a 90-day patient list. A colleague says none of 247 CMR 6.13 applies to them at all. Who is right?
steps: Confirm that 247 CMR 6.13(3) does name institutional sterile compounding pharmacies alongside sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding and non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacies.

Then read on to 247 CMR 6.13(7), which states that the provisions in 247 CMR 6.13(3) and 247 CMR 6.13(4) are not required for institutional sterile compounding pharmacies. The carve-out sits after the list and undoes it for this one type.
Read the carve-out narrowly, because it names exactly two subsections. It does not reach 247 CMR 6.13(1), 247 CMR 6.13(5) or 247 CMR 6.13(6).

So the 14-day certified written notice with the full six particulars still runs, the duty to transfer patient files on request in a timely manner still runs, and because this is a Massachusetts licensee rather than a non-resident pharmacy, the post-closure submission of the original licence or licences, the controlled substances registration and the attestation within 14 days of closure still runs.
worked_examples.resolution: Both are wrong, in opposite directions. The director is chasing a continuity-of-care pharmacy and a 90-day patient list that 247 CMR 6.13(7) has excused, and the colleague is discarding the whole of 247 CMR 6.13 when the carve-out names only subsections (3) and (4). The error the scenario invites is reading a list without reading the exception that follows it, or over-correcting once the exception is found.

worked_examples.scenario: A closing Massachusetts pharmacy will move its controlled stock to a sister pharmacy licensed by the Board. Certified notice with every required particular goes to the Board on day 1. The owner schedules the physical move for day 10 because the movers are available, plans to file the confirming attestation on day 20 counting from the notice, and intends to keep a small quantity of one Schedule VI product for a few days afterwards to finish a patient's course.
steps: Apply the waiting period. 247 CMR 6.14(2) permits the transfer no sooner than 14 days following notification, so a day 10 move is inside the window regardless of the movers' calendar.

Scope the inventory taken on the transfer date. It is a complete inventory of all controlled substances in Schedules II through V and all Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program, so the Schedule VI product is inside the count, not beside it.

Check the signatures. The pharmacist Manager of Record of the transferor and of the transferee both sign the controlled substances inventory report; a staff pharmacist signs only in place of a transferor Manager unavailable through death, serious illness or termination, and only on notice to the Board of the reason.

Run the second clock from the right event. Both pharmacies file an attestation with the Board confirming the controlled substance inventory within ten days of the transfer, not within any period measured from the notice.

Apply the closing prohibition. Under 247 CMR 6.14(2)(f) the transferor pharmacy may not possess any controlled substances after the date of transfer, and 247 CMR 6.14(1) frames the transferred class as Schedules II through VI, so the retained product is exactly what the subsection forbids.

Keep the paper. Both pharmacies maintain a readily retrievable copy of the inventory report for at least two years or as otherwise required by law, and the transferee keeps the records it receives on the transfer date for at least two years.
worked_examples.resolution: Three separate errors, and each is one the numbers invite: moving on day 10 compresses a 14-day waiting period into a scheduling preference, dating the attestation from the notice carries the 14-day figure forward onto a ten-day duty that runs from the transfer, and holding back a residual Schedule VI product ignores a prohibition written without any de minimis allowance.

worked_examples.scenario: A non-resident pharmacy licensed by the Board and dispensing into Massachusetts will shut down. Its compliance officer diaries a task to mail the original licence and a controlled-substance disposal attestation to the Board ten days after the last day of business, and decides not to write to Massachusetts patients on the view that the pharmacy is licensed and located in another state. What should be reversed?
steps: Start with the notice that is owed. 247 CMR 6.13(2) requires a non-resident pharmacy to notify the Board in writing, by certified mail, at least 14 days before the intended closure, unless otherwise authorized, with four particulars: name, address and telephone number, the pharmacy licence number, the intended closure date, and verification that adequate advance notice has been given to Massachusetts customers.

Read the fourth particular as the answer on patients. It verifies notice given in accordance with 247 CMR 6.13(4), and 6.13(4) closes by requiring a non-resident drug store pharmacy, a non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy and a non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy to notify all Massachusetts patients of the closure. Skipping patients therefore fails twice, once on the notice and once on the verification inside it.

Now read the last sentence of 247 CMR 6.13(6): the provisions in 247 CMR 6.13(6) shall not apply to non-resident pharmacies. The post-closure submission of the original credentials with the disposal attestation is the one duty on the officer's list that does not run.

Note what the shorter 6.13(2) list drops relative to 6.13(1): the controlled substance registration number, the Manager of Record's name, and the statement of intended controlled-substance disposal or transfer procedures.
worked_examples.resolution: The diary entry is an exact inversion. The officer has scheduled the single duty that 247 CMR 6.13(6) says does not apply to non-resident pharmacies while dropping the advance certified notice and the Massachusetts patient notice that do apply. The error the scenario invites is treating non-resident status as a general exemption rather than a specific one.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: How long before the intended closure must the written closure notice reach the Board, by what method, and what qualifies the period?
retrieval_prompts.answer: At least 14 days before the intended closure, in writing by certified mail, unless otherwise authorized by the Board (247 CMR 6.13(1), and 6.13(2) for a non-resident pharmacy).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Two of the six particulars in 247 CMR 6.13(1) look outside the pharmacy's own identity. Name them.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Verification that adequate advance notice of the closure has been given to customers in accordance with 247 CMR 6.13(4), and the intended procedures for disposal or transfer of controlled substances.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which patients must a closing pharmacy identify, and over what period?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Each patient who had a prescription filled at the pharmacy within the preceding 90 days of the intended closure date.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: By when and by what method must patient notice be attempted?
retrieval_prompts.answer: At least 14 days prior to the closure date, by first class mail or other Board approved method. The duty is to attempt notice.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Besides the fact of the closure, what must the conspicuous posted notice tell patients?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The procedure for requesting a transfer of patient file information.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What two things go to the Board within 14 days of closure, and which pharmacies never owe them?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The original licence or licences and the controlled substances registration, plus an attestation that all controlled substances were disposed of or transferred by the routes named. 247 CMR 6.13(6) does not apply to non-resident pharmacies.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which pharmacies must identify a continuity-of-care pharmacy, and what must be true of the one they name?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding and non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacies. The pharmacy named must be licensed by the Board and be suitable and available to provide continuity of care.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: 247 CMR 6.13(7) excuses institutional sterile compounding pharmacies from which provisions, and what does it leave standing?
retrieval_prompts.answer: From 247 CMR 6.13(3) and 247 CMR 6.13(4) only. It does not name 6.13(1), 6.13(5) or 6.13(6), so the certified notice, the patient-file transfer duty and the post-closure submission remain.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What exactly is inventoried on the date of a 247 CMR 6.14 transfer?
retrieval_prompts.answer: All controlled substances in Schedules II through V, and all Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Give the three periods in 247 CMR 6.14 and say what each attaches to.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 14 days of certified written notice before the transfer, ten days after the transfer for the attestation filed by both pharmacies, and at least two years of readily retrievable retention of the inventory report.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Who signs the controlled substances inventory report, and what single substitution does the regulation allow?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Both pharmacist Managers of Record. A staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign in place of a transferor Manager of Record unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, provided the Board is notified why.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: What may the transferor pharmacy hold after the date of transfer?
retrieval_prompts.answer: No controlled substances at all.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which closure clock runs forwards from the closure date rather than backwards from it?
retrieval_prompts.answer: The 247 CMR 6.13(6) submission: the original credentials and the disposal or transfer attestation are due within 14 days of closure.

quick_review.text: 247 CMR 6.13(1): a Massachusetts pharmacy and a Manager of Record intending to close notify the Board in writing, by certified mail, at least 14 days before the intended closure, unless otherwise authorized by the Board.

The six 6.13(1) particulars are the pharmacy's name, address and telephone number; the pharmacy licence and controlled substance registration numbers; the pharmacist Manager of Record's name; the intended closure date; verification of adequate advance notice to customers under 6.13(4); and the intended procedures for disposal or transfer of controlled substances.

247 CMR 6.13(4): identify each patient who had a prescription filled within the preceding 90 days of the intended closure date, attempt notice at least 14 days prior by first class mail or other Board approved method, and post a conspicuous notice covering the closure and how to request a transfer of patient file information.
247 CMR 6.13(5): upon patient request, or as required by law or contract, patient files go to another pharmacy in a timely manner to meet patient needs.

247 CMR 6.13(6): within 14 days of closure the licensee and Manager of Record submit the original licence or licences and controlled substances registration plus an attestation of lawful disposal or transfer, and the subsection does not apply to non-resident pharmacies.

247 CMR 6.13(2): a non-resident pharmacy owes the same 14-day certified notice with a shorter list, being name, address and telephone number, the pharmacy licence number, the closure date, and verification of advance notice to Massachusetts customers.

247 CMR 6.13(3): sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding, non-resident sterile compounding and non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacies must additionally notify the Board, at least 14 days ahead, of the identity of a Board-licensed pharmacy suitable and available to provide continuity of care.
247 CMR 6.13(7): the provisions in 247 CMR 6.13(3) and 247 CMR 6.13(4) are not required for institutional sterile compounding pharmacies, and no other subsection is named.

247 CMR 6.14(1): certified written notice to the Board at least 14 days before transferring Schedules II through VI from one Board-licensed pharmacy to another, naming both pharmacies, both sets of licence and registration numbers, both Managers of Record, the transfer date and the security procedures.

247 CMR 6.14(2): transfer no sooner than 14 days after notification; inventory on the transfer date covering Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI; both Managers of Record sign; both pharmacies attest within ten days; both retain readily retrievable copies for at least two years; and the transferor may possess no controlled substances after the transfer date.

decision_logic.condition: A pharmacy licensed by the Board fixes a closure date.
decision_logic.action: Start the Board notice, the patient identification and notice, and the disposition of the controlled stock together rather than in sequence, because 247 CMR 6.13(1)(e) and (f) require the Board notice to report on the other two.

decision_logic.condition: You are drafting the closure notice to the Board.
decision_logic.action: Ask first whether the pharmacy is a Massachusetts or a non-resident pharmacy: 247 CMR 6.13(1) demands six particulars, 247 CMR 6.13(2) four, and the shorter list drops the controlled substance registration number, the Manager of Record's name and the controlled-substance procedures.

decision_logic.condition: The closing pharmacy compounds sterile or complex non-sterile preparations.
decision_logic.action: Add the 247 CMR 6.13(3) notification at least 14 days ahead identifying a Board-licensed pharmacy suitable and available to provide continuity of care, unless the pharmacy is an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy, which 247 CMR 6.13(7) excuses from 6.13(3) and 6.13(4).

decision_logic.condition: You are fixing the population of patients to write to.
decision_logic.action: Take everyone who had a prescription filled in the 90 days preceding the intended closure date, attempt notice at least 14 days ahead by first class mail or other Board approved method, and post the conspicuous notice explaining how to request a file transfer.

decision_logic.condition: A patient asks for their records once the closure is announced.
decision_logic.action: Transfer the patient file to another pharmacy in a timely manner to meet the patient's needs, as 247 CMR 6.13(5) requires on request or where law or contract requires it.

decision_logic.condition: The controlled stock has to go somewhere.
decision_logic.action: Pick the route the attestation will have to name: disposal in accordance with the federal disposal regulation cited in 247 CMR 6.13(6)(b), or transfer in accordance with 21 CFR 1301.52 and 247 CMR 6.14 to another pharmacy licensed by the Board.

decision_logic.condition: The stock is moving to another Board-licensed pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Send the 247 CMR 6.14(1) certified notice with all eight particulars at least 14 days ahead, wait out the 14 days, inventory Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI on the transfer date, have both Managers of Record sign, file the attestation within ten days of the transfer, keep the report readily retrievable for at least two years, and hand over every controlled substance.

decision_logic.condition: The pharmacy has closed and is not a non-resident pharmacy.
decision_logic.action: Within 14 days of closure send the Board the original licence or licences and the controlled substances registration together with the attestation of lawful disposal or transfer.

ma_vs_federal.text: Massachusetts does not write its own destruction procedure into the closure rule. 247 CMR 6.13(6)(b) requires an attestation that the controlled substances were disposed of in accordance with the federal disposal regulation it cites, so what the Board demands is proof that the federal route was followed rather than a separate state method.

For the transfer route the same subsection is cumulative rather than alternative: it speaks of controlled substances transferred in accordance with 21 CFR 1301.52 and 247 CMR 6.14, so satisfying the federal provision does not discharge the state procedure with its 14-day notice, dual signatures, ten-day attestation and bar on post-transfer possession.

The federal citations inside 247 CMR 6.13(6)(b) describe what the attestation must be able to say; the operative Massachusetts duty is the filing itself, made to the Board within 14 days of closure together with the surrendered credentials.

exceptions.text: The 14-day periods in 247 CMR 6.13(1), 6.13(2), 6.13(3) and 6.14(1) are each stated unless otherwise authorized by the Board, so the Board may authorise a different arrangement; the pharmacy cannot shorten them on its own.
The 14-day patient-notice period in 247 CMR 6.13(4) carries no such qualifier, though the method admits first class mail or other Board approved method.
247 CMR 6.13(6) does not apply to non-resident pharmacies, so the post-closure surrender of credentials and the closure attestation are not owed by them.
247 CMR 6.13(7) excuses institutional sterile compounding pharmacies from 247 CMR 6.13(3) and 247 CMR 6.13(4), and from nothing else.

A staff pharmacist may be authorized to sign the 247 CMR 6.14 inventory report in place of a transferor Manager of Record unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, provided the Board is notified as to why.
Patient files move under 247 CMR 6.13(5) upon patient request or as required by law or contract, rather than automatically on closure.
The 247 CMR 6.14 retention floor is at least two years or as otherwise required by law, so a longer period imposed elsewhere in law governs instead.

timing_deadlines.event: Written closure notice to the Board by certified mail
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the intended closure, unless otherwise authorized by the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: A notice sent later, or sent by some other method, does not satisfy 247 CMR 6.13(1).

timing_deadlines.event: Non-resident pharmacy's closure notice to the Board
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the intended closure, by certified mail, unless otherwise authorized
timing_deadlines.consequence: The period matches the resident one; only the list of particulars is shorter under 247 CMR 6.13(2).

timing_deadlines.event: Continuity-of-care notification by a compounding pharmacy under 247 CMR 6.13(3)
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the intended closure
timing_deadlines.consequence: It is an additional notification identifying a Board-licensed pharmacy, not a substitute for the closure notice.

timing_deadlines.event: Attempted notice to each identified patient
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days prior to the closure date
timing_deadlines.consequence: The attempt is what 247 CMR 6.13(1)(e) later verifies to the Board, so it cannot be scheduled after the Board notice.

timing_deadlines.timeframe: The 90 days preceding the intended closure date
timing_deadlines.consequence: It fixes who must be written to; it is a look-back and not a notice period.

timing_deadlines.event: Submission of original credentials with the disposal or transfer attestation
timing_deadlines.consequence: This is the only closure clock that runs after the date, and 247 CMR 6.13(6) does not apply to non-resident pharmacies.

timing_deadlines.event: Written certified-mail notice of an intended controlled-substance transfer
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least 14 days before the intended transfer, unless otherwise authorized by the Board
timing_deadlines.consequence: The transfer may proceed no sooner than 14 days following the notification, so the notice starts a waiting period.

timing_deadlines.event: Attestation confirming the controlled substance inventory
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within ten days of the transfer, filed by both pharmacies
timing_deadlines.consequence: Counting it from the notice rather than from the transfer is the standard error, and ten days is not 14.

timing_deadlines.event: Retention of the controlled substances inventory report and the received records
timing_deadlines.timeframe: At least two years, or as otherwise required by law
timing_deadlines.consequence: Both pharmacies keep a readily retrievable copy of the report, and the transferee keeps the records it received on the transfer date.

forms_records.text: The 247 CMR 6.13(1) closure notice carries the pharmacy's name, address and telephone number, the pharmacy licence and controlled substance registration numbers, the pharmacist Manager of Record's name, the intended closure date, verification of adequate advance notice to customers under 6.13(4), and the intended procedures for disposal or transfer of controlled substances.

The 247 CMR 6.13(2) non-resident closure notice carries only the name, address and telephone number, the pharmacy licence number, the intended closure date, and verification of advance notice to Massachusetts customers.
The notice posted in a conspicuous location at the pharmacy states the intended closure and the procedure for requesting a transfer of patient file information.
The post-closure package to the Board is the original licence or licences and the controlled substances registration, together with the attestation of disposal or transfer.

The 247 CMR 6.14(1) transfer notice names both pharmacies with address and telephone number, both pharmacy licence and controlled substances registration numbers, both Managers of Record with their pharmacist licence numbers, the date the transfer will take place, and the security procedures for the transfer.
The controlled substances inventory report is signed by the pharmacist Manager of Record of each pharmacy and kept readily retrievable by both for at least two years or as otherwise required by law.

role_duties.role: Massachusetts pharmacy and its Manager of Record
role_duties.duty: Notify the Board in writing by certified mail at least 14 days before the intended closure, with all six particulars required by 247 CMR 6.13(1).

role_duties.role: Licensee or Manager of Record of a closing pharmacy
role_duties.duty: Identify every patient who had a prescription filled in the preceding 90 days, attempt notice at least 14 days before the closure date by first class mail or other Board approved method, and post the conspicuous notice.

role_duties.role: Licensee or Manager of Record holding patient files
role_duties.duty: Transfer patient files to another pharmacy in a timely manner to meet patient needs, upon patient request or as law or contract requires.

role_duties.role: Licensee and Manager of Record after closure
role_duties.duty: Submit the original licence or licences and the controlled substances registration with the disposal or transfer attestation within 14 days of closure.
Give the same 14-day certified notice with the shorter 247 CMR 6.13(2) particulars and notify all Massachusetts patients, while owing no post-closure submission under 247 CMR 6.13(6).

role_duties.role: Sterile, complex non-sterile and non-resident compounding pharmacy
role_duties.duty: Notify the Board at least 14 days ahead of the identity of a pharmacy licensed by the Board that is suitable and available to provide continuity of care to its patients.

Take the complete inventory on the transfer date, sign the report, file the attestation within ten days, keep a readily retrievable copy for at least two years, and hold no controlled substances after the transfer date.
Sign the inventory report, receive the controlled substances and the inventory records on the transfer date, file the ten-day attestation and retain those records for at least two years.

common_traps.text: Running every closure duty off a single deadline. The Board notice, the patient notice and the continuity-of-care notification all look backwards from the closure date, while the surrender of credentials and the closure attestation look forwards from it.

Sending a 247 CMR 6.13(1) notice that identifies the pharmacy but neither verifies the customer notice nor states the intended controlled-substance disposal or transfer procedure. Two of the six particulars are about the other duties.

Treating patient notice as an outcome to be achieved. 247 CMR 6.13(4) requires the pharmacy to attempt notice by first class mail or other Board approved method, which is why the conspicuous posted notice sits alongside it.
Applying the post-closure submission to a non-resident pharmacy. 247 CMR 6.13(6) closes by saying that it does not apply to non-resident pharmacies at all.
Treating an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy as excused from the whole of 247 CMR 6.13. Subsection (7) names 6.13(3) and 6.13(4) and stops there.
Carrying the 14-day figure into the transfer attestation. It is due within ten days of the transfer, and the 14 days belongs to the certified notice that precedes the move.
Reading the transfer-date inventory as Schedules II through V. Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program are inside the count.
Letting the transferor keep a residual stock to finish outstanding prescriptions. 247 CMR 6.14(2)(f) leaves the transferor with no controlled substances after the date of transfer.
Merging the closure attestation with the transfer attestation. They have different filers, different deadlines and different content, and a transfer produces both.

authority.name: Advance Board notice of pharmacy closure

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A resident pharmacy generally must give the Board written certified-mail notice at least 14 days before intended closure and provide the required closure and controlled-substance information.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A closing pharmacy identifies patients served in the preceding 90 days, attempts notice at least 14 days before closure, posts conspicuous notice, and supports timely patient-file transfer.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Controlled substances and credentials after pharmacy closure

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Within 14 days after closure, the resident pharmacy submits original licenses and controlled-substance registration plus an attestation of lawful controlled-substance disposal or transfer.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A NON-RESIDENT pharmacy closing gives the Board certified written notice at least 14 days ahead with a SHORTER set of particulars, and the post-closure submission of original licences and the controlled-substance attestation at 247 CMR 6.13(6) DOES NOT APPLY to non-resident pharmacies. A sterile compounding, complex non-sterile compounding, institutional sterile compounding or non-resident compounding pharmacy must ADDITIONALLY notify the Board, at least 14 days ahead, of the IDENTITY OF A BOARD-LICENSED PHARMACY SUITABLE AND AVAILABLE TO PROVIDE CONTINUITY OF CARE to its patients. 247 CMR 6.13(3) and 6.13(4) are NOT REQUIRED for institutional sterile compounding pharmacies.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A licensee, Manager of Record or agent intending to transfer Schedules II through VI from one Board-licensed pharmacy to another shall notify the Board IN WRITING BY CERTIFIED MAIL at least 14 days before the transfer, unless otherwise authorized, giving the named particulars of both pharmacies. No sooner than 14 days after notification the transfer may proceed provided that on the transfer date the transferor takes a complete inventory of all Schedule II through V substances and all Schedule VI substances reportable to the prescription monitoring program; both Managers of Record sign the inventory report, with a staff pharmacist permitted to sign in place of an unavailable transferor Manager on notice to the Board of the reason; both pharmacies keep a readily retrievable copy for at least two years; both file an attestation with the Board within TEN DAYS; the transferee receives the substances and records on the transfer date and keeps the records at least two years; and the transferor MAY NOT POSSESS any controlled substances after the transfer date.
exceptions: A staff pharmacist may sign where the transferor Manager of Record is unavailable due to death, serious illness or termination, on notice to the Board
